_note: Where the large things this repository does not carry come from. Nothing here is game data; these are pointers to it. Keep this file FLAT -- one "key": "value" per line -- because install.sh and fetch-web-client.sh read it with sed and there is no JSON parser in the helper container the Windows installer uses. See linux-port/docker/README.md, 'The five archives'.
_placeholders: A value that is not an https:// link, or not 64 hex characters, has not been filled in yet. Every reader checks that and stops with 'the link has not been filled in' instead of attempting a meaningless download.
_fallbacks: Every *_url may be followed by *_url_fallback and *_url_fallback2 holding the SAME file somewhere else. A fetcher walks the list top to bottom and stops at the first one that arrives with the right sha256 -- so a fallback is not a second-best copy, it is the identical archive and it is checked against the same sum. This exists because an anonymous MEGA share answers '509 over quota' once the OWNER's daily allowance is spent, which is a wait of hours through no fault of the person installing. A fallback turns that into a wait of seconds. Leave a fallback empty and nothing changes; the list simply has one entry.
_engine: The browser client's own code: index.html, index.js, index.wasm, index.dev, webfs.js, serve-webfs.py and the m2-ws2tcp binaries for six platforms. Built by linux-port/package-web-client.sh, which holds the authoritative list of what belongs in it -- the first archive was packed by hand without index.dev and the client stopped at 'starting'. Unpacks flat. It carries no game data, so it is a release asset of this repository -- which is why engine_url is DERIVED from engine_version and never maintained by hand. Publishing a new engine is: attach the file to the release tagged v<engine_version>, then change engine_version and engine_sha256 here.
_data: The corpus the browser client reads: 419 content-addressed <32 hex>.bin blocks and manifest.bin, which is their index and therefore travels with them. Unpacks flat. Game data, so it is on MEGA like the server files and never a release asset. Nine of ten fixes are engine-only -- that is what this split is for: a fix costs 17.6 MB instead of 1.75 GB.
_src_server: The server itself: metin2_server+src.tar.gz and metin2_mysql_dump.zip. Everyone needs this, whichever client they choose. Handed to linux-port/fetch-sources.sh as M2_SRC_URL -- that script already knows how to take the two members out of an outer .zip whatever it is called.
_src_client: The desktop client, as players download it. Needed only by whoever offers the desktop client. This archive IS the client -- one unpacking stage, not two -- and it is handed to the existing client-builder unchanged as M2_CLIENT_ARCHIVE_URL, which still writes the server address into it, sets the language and repacks it for the panel's download button. src_client_kind records that: set it to 'ready' if it ever becomes a finished package that needs no builder, and see the marked block in both installers.
_not_downloaded: Reference_ClientSource.zip (147 MB, MEGA) is the client's Visual Studio source. No installed server needs it and no choice in the installer offers it -- it exists for developing the client further. It is deliberately absent from this file so that nothing can be tempted to fetch it, and it must never reach a player: it is what somebody would use to build a cheat client against this exact server.
